- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 75, forecast often drops; if below 65, it tends to rise — adjust for 1–2% lagged momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently misses early “rebound” or “drop” phases after sentiment shifts — add 1–2% buffer for sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model fails to anticipate; apply 1–3% correction in direction of sentiment swing.
